correctness.rationale: PASS: Open adjacency is exactly complement of row-or-column cross, so uncovered set after a legal prefix equals the intersection of its selected crosses. Two selected vertices sharing row/column leave an entire row/column, otherwise two opposite cells; all third moves either terminate at length three or leave exactly one cell, so no fifth move. Exhaustive cases give z3 and z4 coefficients and boundary m=2 or n=2. Classifying minimal four-sets by bipartite matching number<=2 yields two-rows/two-columns families and their rectangle overlap, 4! orders each. A uniformly chosen next legal vertex differs from sampling a uniformly chosen completed history; conditional probabilities follow from the first two moves. Independent exhaustive original-adjacency legal-history enumeration and rational policy checks for 2<=m,n<=4 passed.
